subcompetencies.name: Pediatric Pre-Anesthetic Patient Evaluation, Assessment, and Preparation

level_1: Conducts and interprets a history and physical examination, with direct supervision
level_2: Conducts a focused history and physical examination, with indirect supervision
level_3: Identifies comorbidities on a history and physical examination that may require further evaluation, with indirect supervision
level_4: Independently identifies concerning history and physical exam findings that require further evaluation
level_5: Independently identifies a previously undiagnosed condition

level_1: Performs basic pediatric airway assessment
Prepares and incorporates advanced equipment in the management of a complicated airway, with supervision
level_2: Prepares age-/size- appropriate equipment for an uncomplicated pediatric/neonatal airway
Independently devises airway management plans that address contingencies
level_3: Uses the airway exam and identifiable risk factors to formulate a patient-specific plan
Independently prepares and incorporates advanced equipment in the management of a complicated airway
level_4: Manages an uncomplicated pediatric/neonatal airway
Collaborates with the interdisciplinary team to develop an airway plan for a complex pediatric airway
level_5: Devises airway management plans that address contingencies, with supervision
Functions as an expert in an airway crisis for complicated airways

subcompetencies.name: Technical Skills – Pediatric Vascular Access (including Peripheral, Arterial, and Central Lines)

level_1: Obtains vascular access in older children and adolescents
level_2: Obtains vascular access in neonates, with guidance
level_3: Obtains difficult vascular access, with guidance
level_4: Independently obtains difficult vascular access
level_5: Functions as an expert for vascular access

subcompetencies.name: Technical Skills – Pediatric Regional (Peripheral and Neuraxial) Anesthesia

level_1: Describes anatomy relevant to regional anesthesia
Recognizes and manages complications of regional anesthesia, with direct supervision
Independently performs regional anesthesia techniques
level_2: Prepares a patient and the equipment for common regional anesthesia techniques
Develops a patient- and procedure-specific regional anesthesia plan, with supervision
Independently recognizes and manages complications of regional anesthesia
level_3: Describes potential complications of regional anesthesia
Performs regional anesthesia techniques, with indirect supervision
Serves as a consultant on advanced or difficult regional techniques
level_4: Describes indications and contraindications for regional anesthesia
Recognizes and manages complications of regional anesthesia, with indirect supervision
Develops institutional protocol for using regional anesthesia and managing complications
level_5: Performs regional anesthesia techniques, with direct supervision
Independently develops a patient- and procedure-specific regional anesthesia plan

level_1: Formulates an anesthetic plan for an uncomplicated patient or procedure
level_2: Develops an anesthetic plan for a healthy patient undergoing uncomplicated procedures
level_3: Develops an anesthetic plan for patients with well- controlled comorbidities or undergoing complicated procedures
level_4: Develops an anesthetic plan for patients with multiple, uncontrolled comorbidities, and undergoing complicated procedures
level_5: Develops a peri-, intra-, and post-operative plan for a medically complex patient as the leader of a collaborative team of specialists

level_1: Implements an anesthetic plan for a healthy pediatric patient undergoing uncomplicated procedures
level_2: Implements an anesthetic plan for an uncomplicated procedure in a neonate
level_3: Implements an anesthetic plan for pediatric patients with comorbidities for uncomplicated procedures
level_4: Implements an anesthetic plan for pediatric patients with comorbidities for complicated procedures
level_5: Implements a peri-, intra-, and post-operative plan for a medically complex patient as the leader of a collaborative team of specialists

level_1: Demonstrates vigilance during clinical care
Participates in management during crisis situations
Independently anticipates an impending crisis and identifies possible etiologies
level_2: Articulates causes of common peri-operative crisis situations
Demonstrates awareness of clinical care and developments throughout a procedure, including those outside of one’s immediate control, with supervision
Independently initiates management and resolves crisis situations
level_3: Responds to crisis situations as a reliable team member
Anticipates an impending crisis and identifies possible etiologies, with supervision
Leads the health care team in the management of crisis situations
level_4: Demonstrates awareness of clinical care and developments throughout a procedure
Initiates management and resolves crisis situations, with supervision
level_5: Recognizes crisis situations; calls for help
Independently demonstrates awareness of clinical care and developments throughout a procedure, including those outside of one’s immediate control

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of normal anatomic and physiologic features of pediatric patients, from neonates to adolescents
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of common medical and surgical conditions in pediatric patients, from neonates to adolescents
level_3: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of common medical and surgical conditions in pediatric patients and related anesthetic considerations
level_4: Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of complex medical and surgical conditions in pediatric patients and related anesthetic considerations
level_5: Serves as an expert consultant for children with complex and/or uncommon physiology and related anesthetic and surgical considerations

level_1: Accurately describes basic elements of a clinical scenario
Independently analyzes complex clinical scenarios using an organized, systematic approach
level_2: Analyzes simple (or common) clinical scenarios using an organized, systematic approach with direct guidance
Identifies and actively avoids clinical reasoning errors
level_3: Retrospectively recognizes clinical reasoning errors, with guidance
Teaches others how to analyze complex clinical scenarios using an organized, systematic approach
level_4: Analyzes simple (or common) clinical scenarios using an organized, systematic approach, with indirect guidance
Models and teaches approaches to avoid clinical reasoning errors
level_5: Retrospectively recognizes clinical reasoning errors independently

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common events that impact patient safety
Describes departmental quality improvement initiatives
Discloses patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and patients’ families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in department quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional level or above

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies specific population and community health needs for their local population
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of population and community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and participates in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of interprofessional team members
Uses institutional resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Role models effective coordination of patient- centered care among different disciplines and specialties
Advocates for populations and communities with specific health care needs in the peri-operative setting

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: States factors impacting the costs of anesthetic care
Manages various components of the complex health care system to provide efficient and effective patient care and transitions of care
level_2: Describes how components of a complex health care system are interrelated, and how they impact patient care
Practices and advocates for cost- effective patient care
level_3: Documents anesthetic detail to facilitate accurate billing and reimbursement
Advocates for or leads systems change that enhances high-value, efficient, and effective patient care
level_4: Discusses how individual practice affects the broader system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Engages in external activities related to advocacy for cost- effective care
level_5: Explains the impact of documentation on billing and reimbursement

level_1: Accesses and uses evidence in routine patient care
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits the patient’s and patient’s family's preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with the patient’s and patient’s family’s preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Appraises and applies evidence, even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence, to guide individualized care
level_5: Mentors others to appraise and apply evidence for complex patients and/or participates in the development of guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals
Designs and implements a learning plan, with prompting
Considers alternatives to improve performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to performance deficits
Seeks performance data episodically, with adaptability and humility
Integrates performance data to adapt the learning plan
level_3: Actively seeks opportunities to improve
Institutes behavioral change(s) to improve performance
Role models consistently seeking performance data with adaptability and humility
level_4: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals
Independently creates and implements a learning plan
Models reflective practice
level_5: Analyzes and acknowledges the factors that contribute to performance deficits
Intentionally seeks performance data consistently, with adaptability and humility
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others

level_1: Describes when and how to report lapses in professionalism and demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Recognizes need to seek help in managing and resolving complex interpersonal situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying patient care
Serves as a model for professionalism among colleagues; actively solicits help and acts on recommendations to resolve complex interpersonal situations
level_3: Uses insight into professional behavior to take responsibility in professionalism lapses, as well as to identify potential areas for self- improvement
Recognizes and utilizes resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas
level_4: Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Addresses system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_2: Performs most tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
level_3: Takes responsibility for the rare occurrence in which tasks are not completed in a timely manner and identifies strategies to prevent recurrence
level_4: Prioritizes tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in even the most complex or stressful situations
level_5: Designs and implements an institutional systems approach to ensure timely task completion and shared responsibility

level_1: Recognizes the importance of addressing personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
level_2: Lists available resources for personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional factors that positively and/or negatively affect well-being
level_3: Describes institutional resources that are meant to promote well-being
Creates institutional-level interventions that promote colleagues’ well-being
level_4: With assistance, proposes a plan to promote personal and professional well-being
Describes institutional programs designed to examine systemic contributors to burnout
level_5: Recognizes which institutional factors affect well-being

level_1: Communicates with patients and their families in an understandable and respectful manner
Facilitates difficult discussions with patients and patients’ families
level_2: Customizes communication in the setting of biases and barriers with patients and patients’ families
Effectively negotiates and manages conflict among patients, patients’ families, and the health care team
level_3: Actively listens to patients and patients’ families to elicit patient preferences and expectations
Mentors others in the facilitation of crucial conversations
level_4: Explains complex and difficult information to patients and patients’ families
Mentors others in conflict resolution
level_5: Uses shared decision- making to make a personalized care plan

level_1: Respectfully requests or receives consultations
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Maintains effective communication in crisis situations
level_2: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Uses closed-loop communication to verify understanding
Communicates constructive feedback to superiors
level_3: Respectfully receives feedback from the health care team
Adapts communication style to fit team needs
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_4: Clearly, concisely, and promptly requests or responds to a consultation
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
Leads an after-event debrief of the health care team
level_5: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record; demonstrates judicious use of documentation shortcuts
Respectfully communicates concerns about the system
Models exemplary written or verbal communication
level_2: Safeguards patient personal health information
Accurately records information in the anesthetic record and communicates complex care decisions for complex cases

level_3: Communicates through appropriate channels as required by institutional policy
Appropriately selects direct and indirect forms of communication based on context

level_4: Accurately records information in the anesthetic record for basic cases
Respectfully communicates concerns about the system and contributes to solutions
Guides departmental or institutional policies and procedures around communication
level_5: Documents required data in formats specified by institutional policy
